title: Cramer column replacement and determinant identities over any commutative ring
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq1$, $A,B$ square $n\times n$ matrices over $R$ [def-weil-matrix], and $b\in R^n$. Write $A[a\leftarrow b]$ for $A$ with its $a$-th column replaced by $b$, and let $\operatorname{adj}(A)$ be the transpose of the cofactor matrix as in [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity]. With determinant as in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the following identities hold:
$$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B),\qquad \det(\operatorname{adj}(A))=\det(A)^{n-1},$$
and, for every $1\leq a\leq n$,
$$\det(A[a\leftarrow b])=(\operatorname{adj}(A)b)_a.$$
No invertibility or nonzero-divisor hypothesis on any determinant is imposed.
